title: Canonical constants and etale markings of finite smooth projective curve covers
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $C$ a smooth projective geometrically integral $K$-curve, $Y$ a smooth projective integral $K$-curve, and $\nu:Y\to C$ a finite surjective $K$-morphism. Put $F=K(C)$ and $L=K(Y)$, with $F\hookrightarrow L$ the inclusion induced by $\nu$. Let $U\subseteq C$ be an open subscheme such that $\nu^{-1}(U)\to U$ is etale, and let $M\subset C$ be a reduced finite etale closed $K$-subscheme contained in $U$. Put
$$E=\{z\in L:z\text{ is algebraic over }K\}.$$
Then evaluation at the generic point identifies $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ with the specified subfield $E\subseteq L$, and $E/K$ is finite separable. There is a canonical factorization $Y\xrightarrow{q_E}\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, with $q_E$ induced by evaluation of global sections; its composite with $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$ is the morphism induced by the inclusion $E\hookrightarrow L$. With this structure $Y$ is smooth projective and geometrically integral over $E$, with function field $L$. The fibre product $P=Y\times_C M$ is reduced, hence equals the reduced inverse image of $M$, and its structural morphism $P\to Y\xrightarrow{q_E}\operatorname{Spec}E$ is finite etale. Also $K$ is algebraically closed in $F$, and $E\cap F=K$ inside $L$. Finite separable means finite-dimensional with separable minimal polynomials. The marking $M$ and the open $U$ may be empty.

Notions: [def-weil-field], [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: Write $R=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $Y/K$ is proper. It is an integral separated finite-type $K$-scheme, so clause (1) of [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] makes $R$ a finite field extension of $K$. By [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal] applied to $Y/K$ and the identity extension, all local rings of $Y$ are integrally closed domains. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], evaluation at its generic point is an injection $R\hookrightarrow L$ compatible with $K\hookrightarrow L$. We use this injection throughout.

source.place: Tag 0BUG, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections (1),(3); Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; properties.tex Tags 01ON and 01RV for generic evaluation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-stein-constant-field] to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, taking its ground field to be $K$ (the function-field letters of that node are renamed here to avoid confusing them with our constant field $E$). The source is normal by step 1, proper and integral of finite type; the target is integral of finite type, and the map is dominant since $Y$ is nonempty. The specified affine construction gives $B_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and the map $Y\to B_0$ induced by evaluation of global sections, with geometrically connected fibres. Since $R$ is a field, $k(B_0)=R$ under its generic evaluation embedding. The function-field conclusion of that node therefore identifies $R$ with precisely $E=\{z\in L:z\text{ is algebraic over }K\}$, inside $L$. Thus the Stein map is the required $q_E$ and $E/K$ is finite.

proof.text: The inverse of the evaluation isomorphism $R\simeq E$ is the ring map $E\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ defining $q_E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] this specifies a unique morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}E$. Its map on sections followed by the generic germ sends every $e\in E$ to the same element $e\in L$. Its composite with $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$ is therefore the spectrum morphism of the inclusion $E\hookrightarrow L$. Restriction to $K$ is the original structure map, giving the asserted canonical factorization. Apply [lem-pc-global-sections-separable] to the original smooth projective curve $Y/K$ and its field of global sections from step 1: $E/K$ is separable. Together with its finite dimension this is finite separability as stated in the item.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-base-refinement] to $K\subseteq E$ and $q_E$. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the original smooth projective morphism, so $q_E$ is smooth and projective. Its fibres are geometrically connected by step 2. Now [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality], with $v=q_E$ and $B=\operatorname{Spec}E$, says that $Y\times_E T$ is integral for every field extension $T/E$: the unique residue field of this base is $E$, and its fibre is $Y$. Here $T/E$ is arbitrary, including inseparable extensions; this is geometric integrality over $E$. The underlying scheme, generic point and generic local ring have not changed. Hence its dimension is still one and its function field is still the specified $L$, with the $E$-inclusion computed in step 3.

proof.text:
Because $M\subseteq U$, the defining fibre product is also $P=
u^{-1}(U)	imes_U M$. The projection $P	o M$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], applied to the stipulated etale map $
u^{-1}(U)	o U$. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), applied directly to $
u:Y	o C$ and $M	o C$. Since $M$ is reduced, [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] makes $P$ reduced. The reduction of a reduced scheme is itself, so $P$ equals the reduced inverse image of $M$. Composition with the finite etale $M	o\operatorname{Spec}K$ makes $P	o\operatorname{Spec}K$ finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2).

proof.text: Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $b:P\to Y\xrightarrow{q_E}\operatorname{Spec}E$. The equality $a\circ b=P\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ follows from step 3. The map $a$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](3), applied to $b,a$, makes $b$ etale using step 5. Also $a$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], since its source is affine. As $a\circ b$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated] makes $b$ finite. These arguments do not require $P$ or $M$ to be nonempty. If $U$ is empty, $M$ and $P$ are empty and the same base-change and composition statements apply.

proof.text: For $C$, [lem-pc-projective-proper] gives properness and clause (2) of [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] identifies $\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)=K$ through the structure map, since $C/K$ is geometrically integral. Its local rings are integrally closed domains by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-sections-algebraic-constants] with $A=K$, $X=C$ and $R=K$. Its finiteness hypothesis holds with the single generator $1$, and dominance holds because $C$ is nonempty. Its conclusion identifies the elements of $F=K(C)$ algebraic over $K$ with $\operatorname{Frac}K=K$. Finally, if $x\in E\cap F$ inside $L$, its membership in $E$ says that it satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $K$. As $F\hookrightarrow L$ is injective, the same polynomial vanishes already in $F$, so $x\in K$. Conversely both embedded fields contain $K$. Therefore $E\cap F=K$.
